title: Install or recover Mantic
summary: Install matched Mantic programs and provider, explicitly initialize private definitions, register command inventory, or recover a compatible retained release without restoring data.
use_when: The caller authorizes Mantic installation, update, or retained-release recovery.
do_not_use_when: The caller wants to edit expense definitions, restore historical config data, or operate an unrelated product.
outcome: The intended matched release is selected, its provider is readable, and explicitly required initialization and command registration have separate verified outcomes.
effects: Stages and selects Mantic programs and provider. Deployment setup or explicit init can initialize empty default private state. Registration can separately change Chancery command inventory.
authority: The user authorizes installation or recovery. Mantic owns its selectors and state initialization; Chancery owns documentation checks and usage registration.
success: Inspect reports the intended release. Config list reads supported selected state. Installed doctor/product/list/show/resolve expose the intended version-matched publication. Usage registration completes separately.
failure_and_recovery: Stop on foreign ownership, mismatched releases, unexpected current selection, unsupported state, failed explicit registration, or unknown retained effects. Inspect completed changes before recovery; preserve definitions.
privacy: Install/recover disclose no definitions or results to a service. Configuration state remains outside program releases; Chancery usage contains metadata only.
does_not_authorize: Editing configs, replacing populated state, sharing private output, scheduling, taking foreign selectors, editing immutable releases, or using program recovery to restore data.
steps: Inspect target selection with the trusted installer.
Submit ./ci.sh submit COMMIT --deploy mantic from the Cell root. Verify the retained Telete job and deployment outcome. Initialize a separately selected empty database explicitly when required.
Register the selected command inventory, inspect selection, read config list, and verify the installed provider.
For recovery, preserve definitions and select one exact retained compatible release, then repeat relevant checks.
checkpoints: Match supplied program and provider release before selecting it.
Guard the observed prior selection; preserve foreign-owned selectors.
Treat selection, state initialization, usage registration, catalog verification, and calculation success as separate evidence.
adaptation: Use CI and Telete as the sole Cell deployment route. Preserve explicit product-owned retained-release recovery.
Use the same absolute home on isolated installer invocations and select runtime databases separately.
stop_when: A release is mismatched, ownership is foreign, expected-current differs, state is unsupported, registration fails, or retained effects are unknown.

consumers.statement: An authorized local operator or interactive agent follows this procedure to select Mantic releases.

preconditions.statement: Deployment or recovery is authorized. The intended committed source or an exact compatible retained release is available; prior selection and ownership are inspected.

inputs.statement: Submit committed source and explicit deployment products through CI and Telete. Retained recovery takes an exact compatible retained release path, optional isolated home and expected selection.

CI and Telete are the sole Cell deployment route. Submit ./ci.sh submit COMMIT --deploy mantic from the Cell root and add required product updates explicitly. Telete validates, prepares signed programs, executes product instructions and retains job and deployment outcomes. Product-owned bootstrap, platform package maintenance and explicit recovery keep their separate supported interfaces.

outputs.statement: Verified selection and provider publication, optional explicit state initialization, and separate command-inventory registration are the required observed outcomes.

data_semantics.statement: Installation selection does not prove a forecast, config validity, actual funds, or payment success. Program recovery preserves current definitions without restoring older data.

identity_and_units.statement: Opaque release identity and expected-current releases/ID guard local program selection; no monetary or forecast unit is defined by installation.
Program archives retain release identities. Running executable files are regular files beneath Mantic/install/runtime and keep the same actual path across install and recovery.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Checks inspect the selected installation and indexed provider at invocation time. The manager retains its own separate delivery-stage outcomes.

access.statement: Actions use trusted local installers and current-user filesystem access; no daemon, model, network, or schedule is operated.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Inspect before changes, guard expected selection, select matched programs/provider, then verify initialization and registration separately. Failed instructions can retain completed changes.

operational_limits.statement: Stop on mismatched sources, foreign ownership, unexpected selection, unsupported state, failed registration, or unknown effects.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Recover only programs compatible with existing persistent state. This initial release supports schema one; no config-history restoration or older-schema migration is available.

reliances.statement: Installation steps rely on Mantic's declared selection, initialization, compatibility, and recovery guarantees.
